name: 1 Pontypool Place
description: Tour of home & garden designed in 2018 by Nagan Johnson Architects
address: 1 Pontypool Place London London, Greater London, SE1 8QF

name: All Saints Church, Tooting
description: A Gothic revival church of cathedral proportions completed in 1906 by Temple Moore with Italian baroque features from Bologna and Florence. Excellent acoustic design has enabled recordings from London Chamber Choir, Paul McCartney's tribute to Linda, Pavarotti, Placido Domingo, and many more!
address: All Saints Church, Tooting, Brudenell Road, SW17 8DQ

name: Bankside: from arches to alleys
description: Bankside was once a secluded powerhouse of Victorian London, a place that kept industry in and casual visitors out. Today, it boasts a network of arches and alleyways repurposed for public use. Led by a Bankside insider, this tour explores the history and reclamation of the arch as a usable space through an emerging urban trail – including the brand-new America Street redevelopment.

name: Barnard's Inn Hall
description: Barnard's Inn in Holborn dates back to the mid-13th century. It is now the home of Gresham College which has been providing free public lectures since 1597. Over the centuries it has been a law school and home to the Mercers' School. Notable architectural elements include 15th-century wooden bays, 16th-century linen fold wood panelling, and has the only surviving crown posts in Greater London.

name: Boston Manor House
description: Boston Manor House is a Jacobean House built for Lady Mary Reade in 1623 and later owned by the Clitherow family from the 1670s until the 1920s. The House is now open to the public with free entry six days a week. Its beautifully restored historic interiors, including breath-taking ornate plasterwork, are joined by two community exhibition galleries, meeting rooms and an attractive modern café.
address: Boston Manor House, Boston Manor Road, Brentford, TW8 9JX

name: Brentford Then and Now/Brentford through the Ages
description: The walk starts in the Medieval market place, proceeds  through 17th century development and 18th century housing then explores 19th/20th century industrial legacy and striking new 21st century Thames-side regeneration schemes.

name: Broadwater Farm Estate Tour inc visit to New Homes site
description: Join us for a walking tour of Broadwater Farm (BWF) Estate & see up close the first new council homes built on the estate in 50 yrs. The tour will also incl. a visit to the historic England‑listed BWF Mosaic currently being restored, as well as the recently improved BWF community centre. To be delivered in collaboration with BWF stakeholders inc. Residents’ Ass, Harmony Gardens & The Lordship Rec.
address: BWF Community Centre N17, Tottenham, N17 6HG

name: Burlington House: Linnean Society of London
description: The world's oldest active biological society. Founded in 1788, the Society takes its name from the Swedish naturalist Carl Linnaeus whose botanical, zoological and library collections have been in its keeping since 1829.

name: Charing Cross Library
description: The building has had many incarnations since its construction in the 1890s as a woolen warehouse.   It became a home to the Italian Benevolent Society, then a fascist club, a serviceman's club, and now a library with the largest publicly accessible collection of Chinese language books in the UK.

name: Corbett Community Library
description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring , an impressive dome, ornate door handles, some stained glass and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.
address: Corbett Community Library, 103 Torridon Road, SE6 1RQ

name: County Hall Kingston
description:
London Square presents a rare opportunity to live within the sensitively restored former Surrey County Hall, complemented by a striking collection of contemporary new-build homes and commercial areas for hire.

Set in the heart of Kingston, residents enjoy a riverside town rich in culture, green spaces, shopping and dining - all with excellent connection to London and beyond.

name: Creative Connections -  Beyond London Bridge
description: Join our walk to explore the hidden enclaves around London Bridge. Discover the secrets of the riverside and some of Southwark’s lesser-known historic corners. We’ll learn how businesses and residents within this diverse enclave, in a former industrial neighbourhood, are joining forces in response to a changing climate in the bid to reach Net Zero.
address: Team London Bridge, 8 Holyrood Street, SE1 2EL

name: Croydon Urban Room
description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.

name: Culture House
description: Culture House is the first permanent exhibition space for Somali artefacts curated by the Somali community.

name: ETAT Annual Art Exhibition, Thamesbank Community Centre
description: There's a Story in All of Us is ETAT's annual exhibition celebrating the creativity, voices and lived experiences of people at our charity. Discover artworks inspired by memory, identity and storytelling, plus the premiere of our silent film, a comedy about a grand art heist set in Pimlico. See how we use our community hall to foster creativity, connection and belonging. Thursday 17 Sept, 12–8pm

name: Film Locations of the City
description: A walk around places in the City you might recognise (or not) from the silver screen. Visit the impressive sites used in major films, including Harry Potter, Mission Impossible, James Bond, and many more.
address: Leadenhall Market (under central atrium by Lamb Tavern), EC3V 1LT

name: Fitzrovia Chapel
description: Loughborough Pearson's red brick building is unimposing from the outside, but inside is a riot of Gothic Revival design. Golden mosaics reveal the character of the Grade II* listed chapel, built as part of the Middlesex Hospital.

name: Fleet Street Heritage Wall and Sundial
description: The Fleet Street Heritage Wall comprises 86 A3 information panels about the people, places, ideas and newspapers which made the name of Fleet Street famous throughout the world.  From 17th to 20th Sept frequent talks will be given on the sundial and the Heritage Wall, and its innovative design features which will  make it accessible to all comers through web pages, Easy Read pages, and audio files

name: Former Carbonic Gas Works, 142 Lea Bridge Road
description:
Paradise works artist studios in the Old Carbonic Works that is thought to be the birthplace of commercial fizzy drinks in the late 18th Century. It features in the Lea Valley and Hackney Conservation area report found online.


https://hackney.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s68747/240220%20Appendix%20A%20Lea%20Bridge%20Conservation%20Area%20Appraisal.pdf
address: Paradise works, 142 Lea Bridge Road, E5 9RB

name: Garage Gallery E17
description: In 2022 we created an art gallery in the garage below our house in a residential street in Walthamstow village.   We aim to bring art into our community, acting as a resource to support artists on a not-for-profit basis.  By the time of Open House we will have hosted 26 exhibitions in a wide range of media, by both emerging and more experienced artists.

name: Historic Monasteries of London
description: Before 1540 London was home to over 40 magnificent monasteries, priories and nunneries. As a former monk myself I am fascinated by them, where they were and what happened to them.

name: IMPACT Community Arts Centre
description: We are a theatre company for performers and artists with learning disabilities in the West London area. We will put on an exhibition of artworks and costumes at our Community Arts Centre.
address: Ealing Central Sports Ground, Horsenden Lane South, Greenford

name: Ibraaz
description: Ibraaz is a London-based cultural institution for art,  culture and ideas from the Global Majority. Bringing together artists, thinkers, and communities through exhibitions, film, debate, publishing, and multidisciplinary programming, Ibraaz creates a brave space where culture fosters exchange, pluralism, and shared humanity.

name: King's Cross Masterplan
description: The Stirling-prize shortlisted King’s Cross Masterplan established a framework for the incremental redevelopment of this industrial heritage site through a mix of uses and a network of public spaces structuring new urban blocks and knitting the site into its context.
address: In front of Bird Cage sculpture, N1C 4TB

name: Lambeth Town Hall
description: Landmark Edwardian Baroque style town hall  in red brick and Portland stone landmark tower.  Interior has marble staircase and ornate council chamber.  Atrium, reception and courtyard spaces created in 2018. Grade II listed. Winner of RIBA London Award 2019.

name: Lauderdale House
description: Grade II* listed building in Waterlow Park dating to 1582. Original Tudor wooden framework adapted by successive owners over the centuries. Today the House runs primarily as an arts, heritage and education centre.

name: Local legends: stories from Tottenham’s streets
description:
What stories live inside Tottenham's streets, churches, parks and everyday places?
Local legends: stories from Tottenham's streets is a unique storytelling walk that uncovers the people, places  and community histories that have shaped Tottenham. Through poetry, oral history, personal memoir and local heritage, participants are invited to experience the neighbourhood through fresh eyes.
address: Lordship Recreation Ground — main entrance on Lordship  Lane (Lordshi

name: London National Park City Visitors Centre
description: London is the world's first National Park City, and our visitors centre at 80 Mortimer Street is the entry point to hundreds of places to visit and things to do across a greener, healthier and wilder London.

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: Marble Arch Youth Assembly - Celebration Event
description: Rooted in the history of Marble Arch as a place of protest and public assembly, we want young people to consider what democracy looks like, not in a parliament, but in the streets, squares and spaces they move through every day. Who has the right to be here? Who gets to decide? Join us to celebrate their work and see their visions for the future of Marble Arch.
address: CasildART, 32 Connaught St, St George's Fields, W2 2AF

name: Millbank – Incarceration, reuse and renewal
description: This tour will explore themes of incarceration, reuse, and renewal focusing on the Millbank Penitentiary and Millbank Estate in Westminster. The walk will explore where the Penitentiary stood, its architectural style, its chequered history and its conditions for inmates.  The walk will then take in Millbank Estate, its origins, design, and its physical connection with the Penitentiary.

name: Mornington Crescent: a walk through South Camden
description: On a walk that begins and ends at Mornington Crescent station, discover how housing, industry, education, entertainment and social reform have shaped the surrounding area. Along the way, explore how buildings and public spaces have been demolished, adapted and given new lives, revealing layers of Camden's changing social history.

name: Morris+Company | 'Waste Not: Materials, Making and the Circular Economy' Exhibition
description: Morris+Company is an award-winning architecture practice based in Hackney, east London. We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  We place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street, reveal our practice to the public and engage local communities.

name: Museum of Croydon
description:
Explore the Museum of Croydon and Croydon Archives:

- Join the Curator of the Museum of Croydon and the Borough Archivist of the Croydon Archives on an intimate guided tour of our stored, rarely seen collections.
- Explore our current exhibitions with our expert staff, including Grayson Perry's Essex House Tapestries and a brand-new exhibition on Croydon's Architecture

name: North End & Hampstead Garden Suburb Prehistory
description:
Victorian London expanded as far north as Hampstead, beyond which lay the wilds of Middlesex. It was here that from 1907 the Hampstead Garden Suburb was built around what was to become the Heath Extension.
Join Calum Orr, Architectural Adviser to the Hampstead Garden Suburb Trust, on a walk from the hamlet of North End to the Suburb, as we try to understand the landscape at this decisive moment.

name: OmniDe
description: OmniDe is a two floors 100m2 office space conceived as a laboratory where Art, Design and Architecture live together. What we designed is a space that is born from the conversion of an existing accountant space into an architecture office.

name: Ongéan
description:
Ongéan Ecosystem : 
Art Studios, Gallery, Performance Space, Edible Garden & Kitchen. All built and designed with 99% Reclaimed Materials by artist Adam Ge-Saelis.
address: Ongéan, Park Mews, Croxted Rd, SE24 9DB

name: Our Yard at Clitterhouse Farm
description: Come and visit this grassroots community enterprise where old meets new in the form of the historic farm buildings alongside our crowdfunded cafe. Find out how some of these historic buildings have been saved and lovingly bought back into community use, and find out about our future plans.
address: Clitterhouse Playing Fields, Claremont Rd, NW2 1AP

name: Parish Church of St Mary The Virgin Lewisham
description:
The church was rebuilt in late 15th century with some of that work still remaining to this day.							
During the Festival there will be opportunities to self-guide or to join a group tour which will include access to restricted areas such as the crypt and tower. These last about 30 min and will start on each hour with the last starting at 3 pm

name: Past Forward: Where Heritage Meets Innovation | Open studios at DIA
description: Discover an exhibition exploring innovation in heritage through projects and stories with Donald Insall Associates. A curated display and film reveal how design, research and conservation are reshaping historic environments. Visit their Grade II-listed Edwardian studio (1914, Sydney Tatchell).

name: People's Museum Somers Town
description:
A great little museum set in the Grade 2 listed Ossulston Estate - a prime example of pre-war Social housing - based on Karl Marz Hof in Vienna.
Open Tuesday to Saturday 10am-5pm, plus Sunday 13th 12am-4pm.

name: Preedy Glass
description: An industrial building originally built for maintaining railways with a modern rear extension now housing a modern glass processing company

name: RAF Biggin Hill Museum & Chapel Tour
description: Join us for an internal and external tour of RAF Biggin Hill Museum and Chapel. Come along and immerse yourself in the history of Biggin Hill from the establishment of the airfield to the events of the Battle of Britain. Hear stories of the men and women who fought and worked at RAF Biggin Hill.
address: Biggin Hill Memorial Museum, Main Road, Biggin Hill, Westerham

name: Red House
description: The only house commissioned, created and lived in by William Morris, founder of the Arts and Crafts movement. Much original detail survives, decorated  by the Pre-Raphaelites, and of extraordinary architectural and social significance.

name: Refugees, Radicals and Revellers in Soho
description: Hear about the history of Soho on a walk around some of the sites associated with colourful characters of yesteryear. From Soho's beginnings as a fashionable suburb in the seventeenth century up to the 1950s, I regale you with delicious snippets of history. We end the tour with the option of refreshments at the birthplace of British RocknRoll.
address: Tottenham Court Rd station exit 4, W1D 2DH

name: Resonance FM Studios
description: Resonance FM is a pioneering, non-profit community radio station, with a studio at 7 Risborough Street, Southwark, London. Broadcasting 24/7 on 104.4 FM, DAB, and online, it offers over 100 weekly shows created by volunteer engineers and programme-makers. The station champions free expression and artistic diversity, providing a platform for local and international voices across arts & culture.

name: Sacred Grounds / St Anne's Church and Garden
description: Start your exploration of the Open House Soho Neighbourhood with a shot of coffee, a refreshing cold drink and a bite to eat.  Explore our timeline of Soho, and our existing display on the church's history.   Relax in our calm and welcoming gardens.

name: Sarabande Foundation
description:
Established by Lee Alexander McQueen to support the most fearless creative minds of the future, Sarabande provides heavily subsidised studios for artists across two sites in London. 

The Tottenham site opened in 2023 and sits within two restored Georgian townhouses, part of the historic Northumberland Terrace and in stark contrast to the contemporary stadium next door.

name: Shaftesbury Theatre
description: Built in a Renaissance style with high level Diocletian windows and a prominent grand cupola. In 2016 a new Fly Tower opened followed by remodelling of the auditorium in 2018 and the creation of a new basement space opened in 2022.

name: Southbank Printmakers
description:
We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.

name: St Anne's Church Wandsworth
description: St Anne's Church, a SW London landmark, nicknamed Pepperpot, celebrated its bicentenary in 2024 (Robert Smirke 1824). The church will be open September 15, 17 and 18 for guided tours and exhibits from the archives.

name: St Anne's Church, Kew Green
description: St Anne's Church, Kew Green was consecrated in 1714. Built with the support of Queen Anne it has been a place of worship for the Royal Families over the centuries. The original 'chapel' has been extended many times and the church is now a little known gem in South West London with a fascinating past.

name: St Anne's Church, Limehouse
description: St Anne's Limehouse has been described as 'the finest parish church in England.' Designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor, it is Grade I listed and one of the Major Churches in the Church of England. It is home to a thriving Christian congregation.

name: St Barnabas Church
description: St Barnabas Church is a grade II* listed building with many Arts and Crafts designed features. Including some wonderful examples of stained glass.
address: St Barnabas Church, St Barnabas Road, Walthamstow, E17 8JZ

name: St George's Bloomsbury
description: St George's Bloomsbury is one of the twelve new churches designed and paid for under the 1711 Act of Parliament for building fifty new Churches, and the sixth and final London Church designed by Hawksmoor.

name: St George's Cathedral
description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.

name: St James's Piccadilly
description: St James's Piccadilly is a Grade I listed Christopher Wren church in the heart of the West End. Completed in 1684, and known as the Artists' Church, its interiors include historic works of art by Grinling Gibbons (reredos, organ case and font), postwar Classical interiors by Albert Richardson, and contemporary art by Che Lovelace honouring the 18th-century abolitionist Quobna Ottobah Cugoano.

name: St Mary & St Joseph Roman Catholic Church, Poplar
description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.
address: St Mary & St Joseph Church, Upper North Street, Poplar, London

name: St Mary the Virgin Primrose Hill
description: St Mary's is a Victorian church famous for its second vicar Percy Dearmer who together with Ralph Vaughn Williams produced the English Hymnal in 1906.  We have a rich history of Church Music, beautiful worship and  vestments.  We also have a passion for  social justice within our community.  We were the first parish in Edmonton Diocese to have a woman vicar.
address: St Mary's Primrose Hill, Elsworthy Road, NW3 3DJ

name: St Mary's Church, Battersea
description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

name: St Pancras Church & Crypt
description: The church (1822 - Grade I listed) is an early and important example of Greek Revival architecture in London. Significant features include the caryatids and tower copied from models in Athens, and the atmospheric crypt.
address: Euston Road/Upper Woburn Place NW1, NW1 2BA

name: Streatham Hill Theatre
description: As part of the Open House Festival, Streatham Hill Theatre stands out as a significant example of London’s theatrical heritage. Built in 1928–29, it was the final theatre designed by renowned architect W. G. R. Sprague. Opening in 1929, the venue hosted theatre, opera, ballet and variety performances until 1962, with a temporary closure between 1944 and 1950 due to wartime bomb damage.

name: Switchboard Studios
description: Built in the 1950s, this site was originally the head offices for a large consortium of industrial spaces which produced dyes and food colourings. It is now a creative workspace with 26 studios for creative businesses and an event space.
address: Switchboard Studios,, 50 Uplands Business Park, E17 5QJ

name: The Annual Sedici Post Grad Group Exhibition
description:
Now in its seventeenth year, Sedici consists of artists from many countries who are now based across England. Working across eclectic mediums and subject matter, this diverse body of artists shares an independent and contemporary purpose highlighting the ongoing strength of Art being made today. 

The gallery itself is a reimagined, mid-century school gymnasium with original details

name: The Building Centre
description: Explore the Building Centre, a landmark home for architecture and the built environment in the heart of London. Discover its distinctive modernist spaces, public galleries and exhibitions, and learn how the building has brought together architects, designers, makers and city-shapers for more than 90 years.

name: The Cartoon Museum
description: Underground museum. Interior design by Sam Jacobs Studio. Design concept influenced by cartoon and comic narrative techniques.
address: The Cartoon Museum, 63 Wells St, W1A 3AE

name: The City Churches: St Stephen Walbrook
description: Wren's own and 'finest City Church'.  Fantastic architecture with different shapes,  twelve Corinthian columns and covered by huge dome - first of its type. Central stone altar by Henry Moore installed in 1987. Birthplace of the Samaritans.

name: The King's Foundation - Charlotte Road
description: A refurbished factory warehouse, the repurposed space now hosts educational programmes and activities of the School of Traditional Arts and the architectural team of the King’s Foundation. Live demonstrations of traditional arts skills by students and alumni, scheduled talks on KF's architectural projects, and guided tours all await the visitor.

name: The Literary City
description: A walking tour of the City, visiting key areas associated with famous writers, from Shakespeare, Dr Johnson, Oscar Wilde, and many others.
address: St Mary Aldemanbury Garden, Love Lane, EC2P 2NQ

name: The Mosaic Rooms
description: Join a tour to learn about the of the history of Tower House, home of The Mosaic Rooms in Earl's Court. Built in 1872 by Thomas Huggett, the tour will also shed light on the interesting story of its former resident, the impresario Imre Kiralfy. See the building and the traces of its history in this walk-through with a presentation of visual materials about the previously unseen interiors.

name: The Purpose of Light: Exhibition by Misan Harriman
description: The Purpose of Light, Misan Harriman’s landmark photographic exhibition, bears witness to significant  moments, not with judgment or ideology, but with a deep and unflinching empathy for the human condition. Featuring 110 unique photographs, this exhibition is a call not for division, but for togetherness.

name: The West End At War
description: A special exhibition exploring the people and places that shaped the area during the Second World War. Tracing famous figures who made Soho their home, and the ordinary everyday heroes who kept the area functioning and our spirits up!

name: The making of journeys in Greenwich
description: This walking tour explores the stories and development of different ways of travelling through Greenwich Old Town across time. For its distinctive physical, social and historical character, Greenwich offers surprisingly a rich landscape of journey-making. The tour follows routes by river, rail, road and time.
address: Outside Deptford  Train Station, Deptford High Street, SE8 3NU

name: Walk through the Stuart Dynasty and Cromwell’s Republic
description: Come and enjoy a circular 2-hour walk around Westminster, Whitehall and St James’ and hear about the events of one of the most tumultuous periods in London’s history, spanning the years 1603 (the death of Elizabeth I and arrival of James I), through Civil War, Regicide, Cromwell’s Republic, the Restoration right through to 1714 and the end of the Stuart Dynasty.
address: Meet outside Westminster Abbey Gift Shop, 20 Dean’s Yard, London

name: Wesley's Chapel and House
description: A fine example of a largely unaltered modest Georgian house, built in 1778 for John Wesley as his London base. Wesley's Chapel is adjacent and was completed at the same time. The chapel was altered internally during Victorian times, when the men's marble toilet facilities and Thomas Crapper toilets were also added.

name: West Bermondsey
description: The tour examines the changing face of Bermondsey through its buildings, industries, and communities, tracing how the Industrial Revolution shaped the area and how that legacy continues to influence the neighbourhood today.
address: Meet at the heart, London Bridge Station, SE1 9SP

name: Worlds End Studios
description:
The building of Worlds End Studios started life as a factory manufacturing machines for commercial baking ovens; it burned down and the remains were used as the foundations of what we know today.
Two young architects found the ruined site in 1974. They wanted to create a community workspace geared toward designers, one of the first of its kind, in London.
